verdict.rationale: Better Auth is a code-first TypeScript auth framework, so natural-language operation is a fair axis. Its only first-party support is a hosted remote MCP server that gives MCP clients (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) documentation search, examples, and setup help. That lets an AI-native user get natural-language guidance, but nothing shows the product itself carrying out operations from natural-language commands. The MCP plugin (which makes your app an OAuth server for MCP clients) and llms.txt are building blocks or adjacent features and earn no credit. Missing for 10: natural-language commands that actually execute operations (e.g., configuring auth or managing users), documented coverage beyond docs and setup help, and independent hands-on corroboration.
